Raid A Small Streamer With Your Friends

Turn up in a three-viewer stream as a group and be relentlessly positive. It costs nothing and completely makes their night.

Cost
Free
Time
30 min
People
Small Group (3-6), Large Group (7+)
Where
Home, Anywhere
Bring
Nothing in particular

Why this matters

Streaming to almost nobody is demoralising, and most small streamers quit long before they find an audience. Because platform algorithms weight live viewer numbers and chat activity, a handful of people arriving at once has an outsized effect on both the streamer's morale and their visibility. It's one of the cheapest ways to make someone's evening.

How to do it

Find a stream with a genuinely small audience - on Twitch, sort by viewer count ascending within a category, or look at people streaming a game or craft you actually like. Fewer than ten viewers is where this makes a real difference.

Then go in as a group and be a good audience.

What actually helps: - Talk in chat. Ask questions about what they're doing. Silence in a small stream is what makes it feel pointless. - Be specific and genuine. Respond to what's happening rather than generic compliments. - Follow, and clip a good moment if the platform supports it. - Stay a while. Five people who watch for thirty minutes are worth far more than fifty who bounce.

What to avoid: - Don't take over the chat or turn it into your group's private conversation. You're guests. - Don't be weird or ironic about it. Don't announce that you're there out of charity - that's humiliating rather than kind. - Don't mass-arrive and mass-leave. A sudden empty chat is worse than never showing up. - Follow the streamer's chat rules.

Pick a different one each month and it becomes a genuinely fun group habit rather than a one-off gesture.
